chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Ayoub, from Bureyd al-Ajaly, who said:
Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) was asked about a man who raped a woman of her chastity. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should be killed, whether he was married or unmarried.'

key_terms.اغْتَصَبَ: to rape / to seize by force
key_terms.مُحْصَناً: married (specifically one who has consummated marriage)

ai.seo_question: What is the punishment for a man who rapes a woman according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from Al-Kafi, Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) establishes that the penalty for rape (ghasaba) is execution (qatl), irrespective of the perpetrator's marital status (muhsan or ghayr muhsan). This ruling distinguishes rape from general adultery (zina), highlighting the severity of the crime in Shia jurisprudence where the key factor is the forcible taking of chastity rather than the marital condition of the parties involved. The consensus on execution underscores the gravity of violating a woman's honor through force.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father and Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, altogether from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Ayoub, from Bureyd Al ajaly who said,
